rejected.title: Character 'would_stand_again' has no 'no' option while landlord/employer equivalents do
rejected.reason: Spec-pinned UX table: character Q5 is 'Yes / Unsure / Prefer not to say' (ux-reference-checking §6.5, verbatim in the story spec's pinned tables). Re-litigating the UX deck.

rejected.title: Wrong-person URL generated but absent from the documented route family and swallowed by the catch-all
rejected.reason: rc3-4 forward contract, spec-explicit ('rc3-3's landing screen and Q1-No render forward links to them'). Unreachable by real users pre-rc3-5 (no tokens minted). Covered as a note (interim 404 copy).

rejected.title: q_salary lacks the empty-datum fallback every sibling as-stated copy function has
rejected.reason: monthly_income_cents is NOT NULL in the schema (verified in 00000000000001_initial_schema.sql:74 and 20260419000002_add_household_income.sql:26); the as-stated salary is always present by the data-availability matrix.

rejected.title: Amount input field name derivation differs between AmountOrDontRemember and AsStatedAmount
rejected.reason: Internally consistent: each control's renderer and validator agree on its own field names (a_<id> vs a_<id>_amount). Asymmetry is cosmetic naming, not a defect.

findings.title: /reference/* POST/PUT routes missing from csrf.should_skip: a session-carrying referee gets 403 on every answer save and the resend (answer lost, JS falls back to a 403 native POST)
findings.evidence: csrf.should_skip arms: ["apply", _] -> True / ["apply", _, "draft"] -> True / ["apply", _, "continue-link"] -> True / ["apply", _, "draft-erasure", _] -> True / ["dsar", _] -> True / ["erase", _] -> True / _ -> False. No ["reference", ..] arm. csrf.validate: 'case req.method { http.Get | http.Head | http.Options -> handler() _ -> case should_skip(path) { True -> handler() False -> validate_token(...) } }'. validate_token: 'case wisp.get_cookie(req, cookie_names.session(), wisp.Signed) { Error(_) -> handler() Ok(access_token) -> ... x-csrf-token required ... csrf_error_response() 403 }'. Router: 'use req <- middleware.apply(...)  use <- csrf.validate(req, ctx.config.secret_key)' before route matching. The SSR form renders no x-csrf-token; reference_form.js PUT adds none.
findings.detail: Every sibling public POST family (apply/dsar/erase) is CSRF-skipped; /reference is not. A browser holding a valid rt_session cookie (landlord testing their own link, shared device, referee who is also a landlord) hits 403 CsrfInvalid on POST/PUT answer and POST resend. The no-JS POST then renders the 403 JSON error page; the JS PUT falls back to the same. Answer lost. Same registry-omission class as the rc3-2 redact gap this round was mandated to fix.
findings.recommended_fix: Add '["reference", ..] -> True' to csrf.should_skip (the apply/dsar/erase pattern) + a pin in server/test/auth/csrf_test.gleam (reference_route_skips_csrf_test) + a router-stack integration test with a session cookie.

findings.title: Desktop JS path never navigates to the review screen after the final answer saves (no-JS POST and mobile JS both do)
findings.evidence: reference_form.js: 'markSaved(section); if (shouldStep(isMobile)) { var nextId = nextQuestionId(orderedIds, questionId); if (nextId) { showOnly(nextId); } else { root.location.assign("/reference/" + tokenFromPath()); } }' - the desktop branch (isMobile false) does nothing after the last save. The form page renders no review link; the page URL carries ?q= so a reload re-renders the form, not the review.
findings.detail: A desktop+JS referee who answers every question has no in-page path to the review screen (where the rc3-4 submit lives); only an accidental Back press or manual URL edit reaches it. No-JS desktop (POST 303 to the bare URL) and mobile JS (location.assign) both work.
findings.recommended_fix: After the final save, also navigate (or render a 'Review your answers' link on the form page) when not stepping: location.assign('/reference/' + token) on the last question regardless of viewport.

findings.title: Validation-error re-render discards the referee's submitted answer (the /apply view_form_with_errors precedent preserves input)
findings.location: server/src/reference_checks/form_handler.gleam:save_answer_from_post Error(reason) branch -> render_form_page(prefill from DB draft only)
findings.evidence: form_handler.gleam: 'Error(reason) -> { let message = ...; render_form_page(token:, slot:, vars:, draft:, current_id: q.id, error_question: Some(q.id), error_message: message) }' - draft comes from 'questions.decode_draft(row.draft_answers)', never the submitted values. The cited precedent preserves: application/form_pages.gleam 'pub fn view_form_with_errors(vacancy, errors, values: List(#(String, String)), posthog_api_key) ' - takes the submitted values.
findings.detail: On a no-JS POST validation failure the question re-renders from the saved draft: the just-typed value is gone while the inline error says 'Check it and try again'. The /apply precedent preserves submitted values. Reachable via too-long other-text, crafted values, or a browser quirk on type=month.
findings.recommended_fix: Thread the submitted field values through the error re-render (prefill the failing question with the submitted values, the view_form_with_errors shape).

findings.title: Autosave DOM choreography has zero automated coverage; the JS comment claims bug-hunt E2E scenarios that do not exist
findings.evidence: reference_form.test.js header: 'Covers the pure seams of the RC3.3 enhancement... The DOM choreography (hide/show, fetch wiring) is covered E2E by bug-hunt scenarios.' - the scenarios directory contains no reference-form scenario (grep: only apply-form/workflow scenarios). Tests cover only nextQuestionId/clampFocusSeconds/shouldStep.
findings.detail: The fetch/PUT/409-reload/POST-fallback wiring is the riskiest JS surface and it is unpinned; the claimed E2E coverage does not exist. The form_draft.js wiring-test precedent (form_draft_wiring.test.js) was not followed.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a node wiring test (jsdom-style, the form_draft_wiring precedent) or a bug-hunt scenario before relying on this path in production.

findings.title: PUT /reference/:token/answer error contract untested: only the 200 happy path is pinned, while the JS keys its reload behavior off 409/404
findings.evidence: Integration: only 'answer_put_autosaves_json_test' exercises handle_answer_put, asserting 200 + persisted. No test for decode-fail 400, invalid 400, unknown 404, closed 409, honeypot/timing fake-ok 200. reference_form.js: 'if (res.status === 409 || res.status === 404) { root.location.assign(...) }'.
findings.detail: The JS autosave path depends on the 409/404 contract to route closed/unknown states to the truthful reload; a regression there would silently misbehave. Bot-guard branches of the PUT are also unpinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin the PUT status contract (400/404/409/bot-200 with nothing persisted) in the integration suite.

findings.title: No fetch/FormData capability gate: in a fetch-less JS environment the submit is swallowed with no native-POST fallback (dead answer form)
findings.evidence: onSubmit: 'event.preventDefault(); ... var data = new root.FormData(form); data.forEach(...); fetch(form.action, {...})' - a synchronous ReferenceError (fetch undefined) after preventDefault kills the submission; the .catch only handles async failures.
findings.detail: The file's contract is 'Progressive enhancement ONLY: without this file the form is fully usable' - but WITH the file in a pre-fetch environment the form is dead. Marginal in practice (fetch is universal since ~2017; a connect-src CSP block is caught by .catch and falls back), but the gate is one line.
findings.recommended_fix: Guard initBrowser (or onSubmit) with 'typeof root.fetch === "function"' and skip interception when absent.

findings.title: Answer-timing stale cap (7 days) is shorter than the link TTL (10 days): a legitimate slow referee's answers are silently dropped with fake success
findings.evidence: is_answer_timing_suspicious: 'delta_ms < 500 || delta_ms > 604_800_000' (7 days). Link TTL: remint_form_token.sql 'form_token_expires_at = now() + interval \'10 days\''. Silent drop: handle_answer_post/put route timing-suspicious to fake success (303 fake-advance / 200 {'ok':true}) with nothing persisted.
findings.detail: A referee who opens the form and answers from a >7-day-old tab (link still valid for 10 days) is classified suspicious: the answer is dropped and the JS shows 'Saved' / the POST fake-advances. Decision 12 adapted the fast floor but the stale cap was carried over unexamined from the /apply one-sitting posture.
findings.recommended_fix: Raise the stale cap to cover the link TTL (e.g. >10 days) or re-stamp _form_loaded_at on resume; at minimum document the interaction.

findings.title: Resend delivered-path effects unpinned: remint persisting, old token dying, the reference_call_link_resent audit row, and the resent page are never asserted
findings.evidence: Integration pins only the all-failed rollback branch. The delivered branch (remint persists + audit row + view_resent) is documented as non-hermetic: 'a Delivered outcome needs a real provider 2xx, which the hermetic test env never produces'. Unit pins cover the seams (any_delivered, resend_audit_details) but never execute audit_resend's create_system write.
findings.detail: The compliance-relevant evidence (reference_call_link_resent audit row on a successful resend) is never exercised by any test; a regression dropping the audit write would pass CI.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin audit_resend's write with a stubbed provider outcome (inject a fake 2xx path or split the audit from the send), keeping the real-provider seam documented.

findings.title: questions.gleam read-side (decode_draft, prefill_for, answer_summary) has zero direct tests: the draft round-trip is pinned write-side only
findings.evidence: grep over server/test/: no test references prefill_for, answer_summary, or decode_draft. form_pages_test passes 'prefill: dict.new()'. The resume integration test covers decode_draft + next_unanswered indirectly only.
findings.detail: The resume feature's read path - revisiting a question shows the saved answer (prefill_for) and the review screen summarizes it (answer_summary) - is the untested half of the A2 contract; rc3-4's structurer consumes the same shapes.
findings.recommended_fix: Unit-pin prefill_for per control kind (round-trip against validate_answer) and answer_summary rendering (incl. the optional free_text empty-string case).

findings.title: Employer/character slot renderers never executed by any test: 2 of 3 slots' question rendering is unpinned
findings.evidence: form_pages_test: 'let slot = LandlordRef ... questions.questions_for(slot)' - the form-page render test builds only landlord question views. The integration seed also uses ref_slot 'landlord_ref' only.
findings.detail: The as-stated employer controls (About right / It differs, salary amount) and the character relationship+capacity pair never render in any test; a broken field name or prefill binding there would pass CI.
findings.recommended_fix: Parameterize the render test over the three slots (or add employer + character render pins covering the distinctive field names/testids).

findings.title: form_pages re-implements the pub brand header instead of reusing application/form_view.view_brand_header
findings.evidence: form_view.gleam: 'pub fn view_brand_header() -> element.Element(a) { html.header([attribute.class("form-header")], [ html.div([attribute.class("header-brand")], [...] Right/Tenantry spans ...) ]) }' - identical markup to the private copy in form_pages.gleam:77-87. form_pages already imports application/form_view.
findings.detail: A third copy of the wordmark markup; the form_view header even documents 'keep the two in sync' - a future wordmark change must now remember three places.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete the private copy and call form_view.view_brand_header() (already imported).

findings.title: month_year accepts non-canonical month strings ("2023-6", "2023-006"), breaking the zero-padded YYYY-MM ordering assumption in validate_month_year
findings.evidence: month_year: 'case string.split(value, "-") { [year_str, month_str] -> use year <- result.try(parse_int(year_str)); use month <- result.try(parse_int(month_str)); case string.length(year_str) == 4 && year >= 1950 && year <= 2100 && month >= 1 && month <= 12 { True -> Ok(value) ...' - string.length(month_str) is never checked. validate_month_year relies on 'string.compare(from, to) != order.Gt' (lexicographic).
findings.detail: Crafted input like from="2026-10" to="2026-3" passes ("2026-10" < "2026-3" lexicographically), storing a tenancy period with from > to, corrupting the draft contract rc3-4 consumes. Real type=month browsers always zero-pad, so this is crafted-input only.
findings.recommended_fix: Require string.length(month_str) == 2 (and canonical re-format) in month_year.

findings.title: Answer-route timing floor is 500ms, not the /apply 2s AC6 prescribes (documented in decision 12, flagged for Perkins in the spec)
findings.evidence: is_answer_timing_suspicious: 'delta_ms < 500 || delta_ms > 604_800_000'; resend keeps the full 2s is_timing_suspicious. Spec AC6: 'timing validation (_form_loaded_at, <2s or >7d suspicious - application_handler helpers reused as-is)'; decision 12: 'Per-question timing floor is 500ms... Flagged for Perkins.'
findings.detail: Deliberate, documented, and fail-closed branches intact (missing/unparseable/future/>7d). The 500ms floor only weakens sub-500ms scripted replays on answer routes; the resend keeps the full posture. Disclosed in the spec itself.
findings.recommended_fix: None required; recorded as a known, disclosed deviation.

findings.title: _focus_seconds is documented as visibility-gated but implemented as raw wall-clock since page init
findings.evidence: Header: 'Maintains the _focus_seconds hidden field (seconds since page init while the tab is visible)'; impl: 'function currentFocusSeconds() { return clampFocusSeconds(Date.now() - initMs); }' - no visibility tracking.
findings.detail: The signal is honestly weak (AD-10) and rc3-4 reads it; the comment overclaims what it measures. Harmless today, misleading tomorrow.
findings.recommended_fix: Either implement the visibility tracking (document.visibilityState listener) or fix the comment to wall-clock.

findings.title: restore_form_token omits the taken_over_at IS NULL guard its paired remint_form_token enforces
findings.evidence: remint: 'AND taken_over_at IS NULL'; restore: only 'AND status = \'contact_initiated\''. A takeover landing between remint and rollback lets restore re-attach the old (always-expired) token.
findings.detail: Belt-and-braces gap only: the restored token is always expired (old expiry), so the classifier renders LandlordHandling for the taken-over row. Truth preserved.
findings.recommended_fix: Add 'AND taken_over_at IS NULL' to restore_form_token.sql for symmetry with the remint guard.

findings.title: stamp_form_opened writes with no status/expiry guard despite its 'first live-form GET' docstring
findings.evidence: SQL: 'SET form_opened_at = now() WHERE form_token = $1 AND form_opened_at IS NULL' - no status/expiry predicate. Handler only calls it from render_live (Live state), so terminal rows are unreachable today.
findings.detail: Defensive-depth gap: the SQL guard is weaker than its docstring implies; a future caller change could stamp terminal rows. Harmless today.
findings.recommended_fix: Add the live-row predicates (status + not-expired) to the SQL for defense in depth.

findings.title: get_form_context_by_form_token selects rc.form_token that no handler reads; the comment's justification is false
findings.evidence: SQL comment: 'form_token itself is selected: the resend flow needs the CURRENT token to build the fresh form URL after a remint.' - grep of form_handler: no read of row.form_token; the resend uses the URL old_token + minted new_token. Generated GetFormContextByFormTokenRow.form_token is dead.
findings.detail: Dead column + misleading comment in the load-bearing context query; harmless but confusing for rc3-4 readers.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the column (and the comment) or make the resend actually read it.

findings.title: Mobile stepper focus() targets the hidden _question input, so the focus move never lands on a visible control
findings.evidence: showOnly: 'var firstControl = current.querySelector("input, textarea, button"); if (firstControl && typeof firstControl.focus === "function") { firstControl.focus(); }' - the first input in every question form is the hidden _question input (form_question_pages renders it first). focus() on hidden is a no-op.
findings.detail: The intended keyboard focus move silently fails; scrollIntoView still runs. Accessibility nit.
findings.recommended_fix: Skip hidden inputs when selecting the focus target (query ':not([type=hidden])' or [data-focus-target]).

findings.title: Mobile gate (matchMedia) is evaluated once at load; viewport changes never re-evaluate it
findings.evidence: initBrowser: 'var isMobile = typeof root.matchMedia === "function" && root.matchMedia(MOBILE_QUERY).matches;' - computed once; no matchMedia change listener. shouldStep(isMobile) is constant for the session.
findings.detail: Rotating a tablet mid-session keeps the initial layout mode. Cosmetic: both layouts remain fully functional.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: listen to matchMedia change and re-apply the stepper.

findings.title: shouldStep unit tests are tautological; the real mobile gate (matchMedia + MOBILE_QUERY) is untested
findings.evidence: shouldStep: 'function shouldStep(matchesMedia) { return !!matchesMedia; }' - the test asserts true->true / false->false (identity). MOBILE_QUERY string and the matchMedia call site are untested.
findings.detail: The seam test proves nothing; the real gate lives in the untested DOM wiring (see the autosave-choreography warning).
findings.recommended_fix: Test MOBILE_QUERY against matchMedia semantics or fold into the wiring tests.

findings.title: SAVED_TEXT / js_saved_indicator cross-file sync is comment-guarded only, with no cross-file pin
findings.evidence: Both sides carry 'KEEP IN SYNC' comments; the em-dash/vocab enumeration includes js_saved_indicator but no test compares the two constants.
findings.detail: Same precedent as form_draft.js (comment-guarded); a drift would only show as a wrong 'Saved' label. Low risk.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: a node test that greps form_copy.gleam for the expected constant.

findings.title: Spec Project Structure Notes omit restore_form_token.sql (ships in the File List; the edge-case fix 2 rollback)
findings.evidence: Project Structure Notes list four new SQL files (get_form_context, stamp_form_opened, save_draft_answer, remint); restore_form_token.sql appears only in the File List. The module itself is documented in the resend flow section.
findings.detail: Docs-only inconsistency in the spec's structure notes.
findings.recommended_fix: Add restore_form_token.sql to the Project Structure Notes.

findings.title: JS test count '118+6' overstated: node --test reports 118 total (the 6 new reference_form tests are inside the 118)
findings.evidence: Ran 'node --test scripts/js-tests/*.test.js': '# tests 118, # pass 118'. The Dev Agent Record says 'node --test 118+6' / '124 JS green'.
findings.detail: The 124 figure double-counts; actual JS suite is 118 green.
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the record.

findings.title: Router wiring of the /reference family (incl. the AC7 catch-all arm) has no test: integration tests call handlers directly, bypassing the route table + middleware chain
findings.evidence: Integration tests invoke form_handler.handle_get/handle_answer_post/handle_answer_put/handle_resend directly with simulate requests; no test exercises the router arms or the csrf/middleware chain. handle_unknown_path has zero test references.
findings.detail: The middleware-chain gap is exactly what let the CSRF skip-list omission slip past a green suite. The catch-all AC7 arm (typo'd links off the SPA shell) is also unpinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a router-stack test (route table + csrf + middleware) for the reference family, incl. a session-cookie POST.

findings.title: clamp_current (?q= deep-link / Back / Change navigation) has no handler-level test
findings.evidence: grep over server/test: clamp_current unreferenced. The ?q= clamp (answered-or-first-unanswered else snap) is exercised only by the integration resume test at the bare URL.
findings.detail: Deep-link positioning is a shipped behavior (Change links + Back) with no pin; a clamp regression would pass CI.
findings.recommended_fix: Unit-pin clamp_current (answered q, unanswered q, unknown q, complete draft).

findings.title: Escape-route + review-submit links render live while their routes are unregistered: clicks land on the branded unknown-link 404 with generic copy (rc3-4 forward contract; unreachable pre-rc3-5)
findings.evidence: Landing links: '/reference/' <> token <> '/wrong-person' and '/decline'; review form action '/reference/' <> token (submit); router registers none of these (rc3-4), so GET hits the '["reference", ..]' catch-all -> handle_unknown_path -> view_not_found: 'This link doesn't look right...'. Spec: 'The exit routes ... -> rc3-4. rc3-3's landing screen and Q1-No render forward links to them.'
findings.detail: Spec-explicit forward contract (same pattern as rc3-2 templates linking here). No real user can reach it before rc3-5 mints tokens. Flag: rc3-4 must land before rc3-5, and the interim 404 copy ('link may have been replaced') is misleading for a wrong-person/decline click once reachable.
findings.recommended_fix: None for rc3-3 (spec'd); rc3-4 registers the routes. Consider routing the interim clicks to a 'coming soon' copy if rc3-3 ships standalone.

findings.title: Pinned chrome 'per-question Save (desktop)' is not rendered: desktop buttons read 'Continue'; save_label is a dead export
findings.evidence: view_actions renders continue_label for every non-identity question regardless of viewport; no CSS/JS swap to save_label exists. Spec chrome: 'per-screen primary Continue (mobile) / per-question Save (desktop)'.
findings.detail: Minor spec deviation: desktop users see 'Continue' per question (functionally identical - each form saves one question). save_label is dead.
findings.recommended_fix: Either implement the desktop label swap (CSS/JS) or drop save_label + note the deviation.

findings.title: form_copy exports other_option_label that no production code renders
findings.evidence: grep: other_option_label referenced only in the copy test enumeration; the ChoiceWithOther 'other' option label comes from opt_other.
findings.detail: Dead export in the copy module (the em-dash test keeps it enumerated).
findings.recommended_fix: Drop it or use it for the reveal label.

findings.title: Hard-coded data-testid 'reference-input-dont_remember' ignores the question id (unlike every sibling testid)
findings.evidence: view_checkbox(qv, field: 'a_' <> q.id <> '_dont_remember', label: ..., testid: 'reference-input-dont_remember') - the testid is constant; siblings derive from the field ('reference-input-' <> field).
findings.detail: House convention drift; only one such control exists today (rent_amount), so no collision.
findings.recommended_fix: Derive the testid from the field name like the siblings.

findings.title: thousands_separated/group_every_three re-implement the codebase's existing thousands-grouping helper
findings.evidence: codebase lens cites content/layout.gleam:405/433 as an existing thousands-grouping helper; form_handler implements its own group_every_three.
findings.detail: Duplicate formatting logic; the salary copy path is the only consumer here. Minor.
findings.recommended_fix: Reuse the existing helper (or extract to a shared formatter).

findings.title: Resend double-submit: the second POST finds the reminted (dead) old token and renders the unknown-link 404 - truthful copy, but an abrupt stop for a double-clicker
findings.location: server/src/reference_checks/form_handler.gleam:handle_resend (lookup NotFound -> render_not_found) / resend_fresh_link 0-row -> redirect to old token
findings.evidence: handle_resend: 'Error(NotFound) -> render_not_found()'; the 2s timing floor + token-death make repeat resends impossible for real humans within the same page load, but a slow double-click after a completed first send lands on the unknown page. Copy: 'the link may have been replaced by a newer one. Check the most recent message from us' - truthful for this exact case.
findings.detail: Handled with truthful copy + contact route; the flow is self-rate-limiting by construction (AD-14). No dead end.
findings.recommended_fix: None required; documented behavior.

findings.title: form_handler.gleam is ~835 lines against the <200-line logic-module target and mixes HTTP dispatch, SQL orchestration, formatting, and copy assembly
findings.evidence: Module spans classifier + GET dispatch + POST/PUT handlers + resend flow + audit + salary formatting + query-param helpers. The spec's decision 1 split pages into two modules ('if either crosses the 400-line view-module target') but the handler outgrew its target.
findings.detail: House line-target drift; the module is still cohesive (one route family). A future story (rc3-4) may warrant a split.
findings.recommended_fix: Defer to rc3-4; consider extracting formatting + review-entry helpers.

findings.title: is_answer_timing_suspicious duplicates application_handler.is_timing_suspicious with only the floor constant changed
findings.evidence: Both implement: missing -> True; unparseable -> True; delta < floor || delta > 604_800_000. Only the floor differs (500 vs 2000). Decision 12 chose the adaptation; the implementation copies the body.
findings.detail: Deliberate adaptation, copy-pasted; a future change to one branch (e.g. the stale cap) must remember both.
findings.recommended_fix: Parameterize the floor into one shared helper (is_timing_suspicious(values, floor_ms)).

findings.title: is_public_path pins omit the /wrong-person and /decline sub-paths the landing page links to
findings.evidence: Pins: reference_form_is_public_test (/reference/<token>), reference_answer_is_public_test (/answer), reference_resend_is_public_test (/resend). The arm is '["reference", ..]' (prefix), so /wrong-person + /decline are covered by construction - but not pinned.
findings.detail: Representative pins suffice for a prefix arm; the omitted sub-paths are rc3-4 routes anyway. Cosmetic.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: extend the pin list when rc3-4 lands.

findings.title: Test fixture 'test-token-48-chars' is 19 characters, not 48
findings.evidence: const token = "test-token-48-chars" - 19 chars. The mint is wisp.random_string(48). Length is irrelevant to the render assertions.
findings.detail: Cosmetic naming nit.
findings.recommended_fix: Rename the fixture.

findings.title: open_vars fixture inconsistency: questions_test clears employment_duration/job_title but not employer_name (form_copy_test clears all three)
findings.evidence: questions_test open_vars: 'form_copy.CopyVars(..vars(), employment_duration: "", job_title: "")'; form_copy_test: also employer_name: "". The AsStatedText open variant keys off duration/title only, so the tests still exercise the branch.
findings.detail: Fixture drift; the q_works_at fallback copy is covered in form_copy_test only.
findings.recommended_fix: Align the two open_vars fixtures.

findings.title: no_banned_error_vocabulary_test matches exact-case 'Error'/'Failed' only; lowercase variants pass
findings.evidence: Test: 'string.contains(s, "Error") |> should.be_false; string.contains(s, "Failed") |> should.be_false' - case-sensitive. A lowercase 'error' or 'failed' in copy would pass.
findings.detail: The brand-voice guard is case-sensitive; hardening opportunity.
findings.recommended_fix: Lowercase both sides before contains.

findings.title: euro_amount accepts leading zeros ("0001400") and possibly '+', storing non-canonical amount_eur strings rendered as '€001400'
findings.evidence: euro_amount: 'int.parse(value)' + 'string.length(value) <= 7 && n > 0' - "0001400" parses to 1400 with length 7, accepted, stored raw. The review screen renders '€' <> a. ("+1400" acceptance depends on int.parse sign handling - unverified.)
findings.detail: Canonicalization gap in the stored draft contract; cosmetic on the review screen, feeds rc3-4's structurer.
findings.recommended_fix: Reject leading zeros/signs or canonicalize (int.to_string(n)) before storing.

findings.title: Em-dash/vocabulary guard relies on a hand-maintained enumeration of form_copy's public surface
findings.evidence: no_em_dash_in_any_string_test iterates all_strings() - a hand-maintained list of every public string (incl. interpolated variants). A new string added to form_copy without updating all_strings() escapes the CI-guarded ban.
findings.detail: The enumeration is thorough today (constants + interpolated variants); the maintenance burden is the risk.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: reflection-free alternative is not available in Gleam; keep the list updated (add a comment in form_copy header).

findings.title: CopyVars test fixtures triplicated across the three new reference_checks test files
findings.evidence: Each file defines its own vars()/open_vars() CopyVars fixtures (with the drift noted above).
findings.detail: Fixture duplication invites drift (already visible in open_vars); a shared helper module would centralize.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract a shared test fixture helper.

findings.title: Bot fake-advance 303s to the bare token URL (landing for an empty draft), a response shape distinguishable from the legit ?q=<next> advance AC6 prescribes
findings.evidence: Bot branch: 'True -> wisp.redirect(to: "/reference/" <> token)'; legit branch 303s to '?q=<next>#q-<next>'. For an empty-draft session the bot redirect renders the LANDING page. AC6: 'silently dropped with a fake-advance (303 to the next question, nothing persisted)'.
findings.detail: The silent-drop doctrine (no error signal) holds, but a bot following redirects can distinguish fake (landing) from real (question). The landing is the design's true next state for an empty draft, so the deviation is minor.
findings.recommended_fix: Fake-advance to the same ?q=<next> target the legit path uses (rendering identical bytes).

findings.title: Landlord compound controls render but their distinctive fields (month-year names, amount, dont_remember) are never asserted
findings.evidence: The render test pins option-row testids + honeypot/timing/focus fields but no 'name="a_tenancy_from"' / 'a_rent_amount' / 'a_tenancy_ongoing' assertions.
findings.detail: A renamed compound-control field would pass the render test (validators would still catch mismatches at the unit level).
findings.recommended_fix: Add field-name pins for the compound controls.

findings.title: Resume pre-fill wiring (checked/value attributes from the draft) is never asserted: the resume test pins only the data-current marker
findings.evidence: The resume integration test asserts data-current + landing absence only; no test renders a question with a populated draft and asserts the pre-filled checked/value attributes.
findings.detail: The read-side prefill behavior (see the read-side warning) is unpinned end-to-end.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend the resume test to assert a pre-filled control.

findings.title: Navigation render pins missing: Start href (?q=<first>#q-<first>) and the Back-link branch are unasserted
findings.evidence: landing_renders_art14_and_both_escape_routes_test pins escape routes but not the Start href; view_question is always rendered with back_url: None in tests.
findings.detail: The deep-link navigation contract (Start, Back, Change) lacks render pins.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin the Start href and one Back link.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS (per-chunk: c1 FAIL, c2 FAIL, c3 PASS, c4 CONCERNS, c5 CONCERNS)
findings.evidence: Tests-lens gates: chunk1 FAIL (JS DOM wiring zero coverage), chunk2 FAIL (router-stack/CSRF path untested), chunk3 PASS (handler+questions write-side comprehensively pinned), chunk4 CONCERNS (slot renderers unpinned), chunk5 CONCERNS (PUT error contract unpinned).
findings.detail: P0 paths of the no-JS first-class flow are well pinned (integration + unit: classifier matrix, guarded SQL, token states, rollback). The JS enhancement path and the middleware/CSRF chain are the drag; both are captured as warnings above. No P0 gap in the first-class path.
findings.recommended_fix: Address the JS-wiring and router-stack coverage warnings; the gate then reads PASS.
